title: KAITEN_Botnet_Incident_Response_Scenario_82f
description: Investigate and respond to a KAITEN botnet incident on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents related to the KAITEN botnet family. Your task is to investigate and respond to these incidents. This scenario will help you develop skills in identifying suspicious services, abnormal traffic, and persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:
- Host: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious systemd timer responsible for periodic external communication?
levels.solution:
Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely responsible for periodic external communication. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers and identify the suspicious service. The flag type is the name of the timer.

**Answer:** system-update-checker.timer

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Start by understanding the types of services that might be responsible for periodic external communication.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers and investigate them for unusual behavior.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for systemd timers making periodic outbound connections.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd timer generating abnormal volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution:
Investigate network connections and look for services making excessive outbound requests. The service generating abnormal traffic is likely responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all network connections and identify the suspicious service. The flag type is the name of the timer.

**Answer:** bot-flood.timer

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Understand the types of services that might generate abnormal volumes of network traffic.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use `ss -tulnp` to list all network connections and investigate them for unusual behavior.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check for systemd timers making frequent outbound connections to the victim machine.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd timer used as the persistence mechanism by the suspicious service?
levels.solution:
Check systemd timers and services for clues about how the service is started automatically. The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd timer used for persistence. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers and identify the persistence mechanism. The flag type is the name of the timer.

**Answer:** system-update-checker.timer

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Understand the different methods that services can use to persist after a reboot.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers` to investigate timers and services for persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for systemd timers that trigger the suspicious service.
